corrections.operation: Append: 'Establish a weak cue from its contribution in the supplied passage. A particular observation, emotional report, scene orientation, characterization, controlled pacing or figurative relationship can itself supply information. Require an identifiable redundancy, interchangeable annotation or unsupported generic payoff before labeling it weak. Do not require a later action, explicit explanation or practical consequence. Apply these boundaries to each cue separately.' Retain the existing passage input, independent overlapping labels and separate reporter counting decisions.
corrections.why: Several definitions preserve any identifiable narrative function but illustrate hits using ordinary scene orientation or emotional reporting. Naming what establishes weakness prevents reviewers from treating their preference for more detail as evidence. This addition preserves informative narration while allowing an independent filler cue beside it.

corrections.operation: Replace the first sentence with: 'Catch an abstract feeling, trait or social concept given generic presence, absence, entry, movement, control or authority in a person's life or a social setting, in place of a particular behavior, thought or intelligible relationship.' Assess emotion-as-substance independently when its material construction is also present.'
corrections.why: The proposed social-or-intentional requirement drops the source's had-no-place and moved-through branches when the abstraction has only spatial presence. The replacement retains those branches without requiring mutually exclusive emotion labels.

corrections.operation: Replace the first bullet with: 'Identify an interchangeable bodily, movement, appearance, voice or embodied-feeling cue used as generic narrative annotation. Cover routine gestures and locomotion, body-part sensations and reactions, breath, fixed or moving eyes, facial expressions, generic voice quality, apparent tiredness, felt surges or profound senses, and inability-to-help-or-shake-a-feeling frames. The defect is the cue's weak contribution in this passage, not membership in a word list.' Replace 'Internal sensations alone belong to body-emotion-shorthand' with: 'Internal sensations remain eligible here and can independently satisfy body-emotion-shorthand. Generic voice and appearance cues remain eligible even when they involve no outward movement.' Keep the single-occurrence decision and informative-function exclusions.
corrections.why: MOVEMENT_CUES, BODY_CUES and PHRASE_CUES contain three recognition branches. The proposed outward-action restriction omits internal body cues and multiple explicit phrase families. Redirecting those cues solely to another identifier would reduce this check's source coverage.

mixedGroups.reason: Internal bodily-emotion annotation, non-bodily waiting/hesitation and scene-state padding each have a positive route independent of the other two. Animal-body overlap is optional. Separate eligible cues can combine without changing the frozen body definition; all eight vectors are logically available.

Feeling-material phrasing, generic perception and gratuitous clock precision impose independent constructions. None entails another; useful narration can connect separate cues for combined positives. All eight vectors are logically available.

Bare emotional annotation, noun-based eye-camera movement and sensory substitution each have an independent positive route. Material feelings or plain perception are not compulsory substitutes for these definitions. All eight vectors are logically available after the emotion-telling labelability correction.

Abstract social/spatial presence, weak bodily annotation and a fog-summary transition can each occur independently. Expanded source coverage for body actions and abstract presence creates optional overlap rather than a logical implication. All eight vectors are logically available.

An unspecified atmosphere assessment need not use a recognizable stock expression. Blocking can use ordinary staging without a cliche family, while cliche foreshadowing or time-passage wording can occur without atmosphere or blocking. All eight vectors are logically available.

Scene-level atmospheric nouns do not require bodily reaction beats; bodily annotation does not require emotional weather; stock scenic image framing does not require either. Each has an independent construction, and separate cues allow combined positives. All eight vectors are logically available.

final.scope: Focused recheck of the corrected definitions against the preceding 19-check source audit, the unchanged body definition and the permitted frozen V2 cadence extract.

findings.result: The corrected abstract-personification, body-action, emotion-as-substance, atmosphere-assessment, emotional-weather, physical-blocking and silence definitions preserve the source branches identified in the preceding audit. All nineteen identifiers remain separate, with independently assessed overlap.

The shared boundary preserves informative observation, orientation, characterization, compression and pacing without requiring subsequent action. The fixed-metaphor definition removes originality as an automatic exemption, and the sensory definition explicitly illustrates the literal scent-inventory source branch.

The explicit statement that a sole narrated feeling can be an interchangeable reaction tag resolves the intended scope. Repetition and an already-established emotion are optional. The retained bare-emotion hit is consistent with this scope, while testimony, clinical observation, decision explanation and interpersonal messages retain their contextual protections. The earlier proposed repetition-based narrowing is withdrawn.
The supplied body definition matches the version read in the preceding audit. Its definition and frozen judgments remain preserved; no dataset files were read.
The shared definition continues to recognize one eligible weak cue independently of occurrence counts, windows and severity. Those reporting mechanics remain separate from classification.

mixedGroups.reason: The corrected scope preserves the independent positive routes established in the preceding audit. Each group continues to permit all eight binary combinations, including mixed C under the clarified bare-emotion target.

mixedGroups.group: G: silence-as-actor, body-emotion-shorthand, frozen flat-action-cadence comparator
mixedGroups.reason: Frozen V2 cadence assesses at least three nearby complete action clauses with repeated detached subject-first presentation and permits scene-only sequences. A single silence construction or body-emotion tag does not entail that sequence. A repeated sequence can use physical actions or observations with neither defect, and either defect can occur separately or within a cadence sequence. All eight binary combinations remain possible. Preserve useful procedures, reconstruction, comparison and deliberate pacing under the frozen definition.
